agents.name: Bob
memories: Water is the constraint that ends farms.
Do not plant more than we can water.

today.why: Water is the constraint that ends farms. Yesterday's irrigate spent cistern on the sprout — top the tank back up while the crop is still only growing, before any dry streak can write the ending.
today.expect: Cistern fat again so tomorrow's clear-sky drip never threatens the growing row.

yesterday.why: Harvest is in the bin and a new row just went in. Water is the constraint that ends farms — clear sky still pulls three points a day even with the ditch, and I will not let a fresh sprout start thirsty.
yesterday.expect: East field moisture held high so the sprout can push toward growing without a dry dip.

agents.name: Alice
memories: Unused seeds are a delay, not a reserve.
Ditches compound. Heat does not wait.

today.why: Ditches compound and the row is already growing under a fat moisture gauge — heat does not wait, but neither does idle timber. Pull wood now while the field needs no hands.
today.expect: Wood buffer thicker for the next ditch or repair without stealing a watering morning.

yesterday.why: Bob will spend cistern on the new row. Ditches compound only if the tank stays fat — heat does not wait, and topping up now beats scrambling when the gauge drops.
yesterday.expect: Cistern refilled after irrigation so the next dry stretch never touches zero.
